## Purpose and topology
OpenReplay is a self-hosted session-replay and developer-observability platform. It captures browser/mobile activity, stores and processes replay streams, exposes management/query APIs, and renders replay, analytics, alerts, and support tools. The repo is a multi-runtime monorepo: TypeScript/React, Go, Python, and Node.js.

## Capture SDKs and protocol boundary
The browser tracker observes DOM, input, console, network, performance, tabs, and optional state integrations; it encodes batches in a Web Worker before transport. The binary/message schema is generated from a shared protocol source, making generated readers/writers a critical compatibility boundary across client, ingest, playback, and connectors.
- `tracker/tracker/src/main/app/index.ts`
- `tracker/tracker/src/webworker/BatchWriter.ts`
- `mobs/templates/backend~pkg~messages~messages.go.erb`

## Ingest and asynchronous processing pipeline
The Go backend is decomposed into independently runnable services. HTTP receives tracker traffic; sink consumes and writes session data; ender finalizes sessions; heuristics derives issues; assets/images/canvases handle replay dependencies. Redis streams and Kafka-related packages provide queue/consumer abstractions, separating high-volume ingestion from persistence and post-processing.
- `backend/cmd/http/main.go`
- `backend/cmd/sink/main.go`
- `backend/cmd/ender/main.go`

## Storage and data access
Persistence is intentionally polyglot: PostgreSQL holds application/control-plane data, ClickHouse supports event/session analytics, Redis supports cache/streaming/session state, and S3-compatible object storage holds replay files and assets. Go storage adapters centralize these infrastructure boundaries.
- `backend/pkg/db/clickhouse/connector.go`
- `backend/pkg/db/postgres/pool/pool.go`
- `backend/pkg/objectstorage/s3/s3.go`

## Control-plane APIs and integrations
The Python Chalice API provides the legacy/control-plane surface for authentication, projects, users, session search, alerts, source maps, notifications, and integration configuration. It mediates external systems including GitHub/Jira, Slack/Teams, and observability providers such as Sentry, Datadog, Elastic, and CloudWatch.
- `api/app.py`
- `api/chalicelib/core/sessions/sessions_search_pg.py`
- `api/chalicelib/core/issue_tracking/integrations_manager.py`

## User application and replay runtime
The React frontend is the operator UI. Routing and state stores invoke service-layer API clients for sessions, dashboards, analytics, alerts, and administration. Its replay engine decodes stored message streams and reconstructs web/mobile sessions; this is a separate runtime concern from UI composition.
- `frontend/app/initialize.tsx`
- `frontend/app/components/Session/Session.tsx`
- `frontend/app/player/web/WebPlayer.ts`

## Real-time and auxiliary products
Assist is a Node/WebSocket service supporting live customer assistance, with WebRTC-oriented client/player components. Spot is a browser extension for recording bug reports. Source-map reading is an isolated Node service. Enterprise adds tenant/permissions, SAML/SCIM, connectors, video replays, and AI/recommendation services.
- `assist/server.js`
- `spot/entrypoints/background.ts`
- `sourcemapreader/server.js`

## Deployment model
Docker Compose supports local multi-service operation; Helm charts deploy each pipeline role independently to Kubernetes with scaling, ingress, and service-monitor templates. The deployed platform depends on Kafka, ClickHouse, PostgreSQL, Redis/Valkey, and MinIO/S3-compatible storage.
- `scripts/docker-compose/docker-compose.yaml`
- `scripts/helmcharts/openreplay/Chart.yaml`
- `scripts/helmcharts/openreplay/charts/sink/templates/deployment.yaml`
